priorities.finding: Request-context features are the only train-only screened group with positive primary lift (+0.002213) and full coverage. The four reported daily lifts are all positive, but the daily standard deviation (0.005804) exceeds the aggregate lift, so the effect is directionally consistent but small and not yet a basis for broader feature-budget expansion. Official validation shows usable within-user ranking evidence (GAUC 0.668912) alongside nDCG@5 0.536958 and primary 0.602935.
priorities.recommended_action: Keep tab, hour, and weekday in the scorer and stop feature screening under the strict early-stopping rule. Treat this as a modest validated gain; allocate any remaining effort to monitoring and calibration rather than launching additional feature-group experiments.

priorities.finding: The main weakness is top-five ranking by tab, not a uniform GAUC failure. Tab 8 has both poor GAUC (0.351852) and nDCG@5 (0.026336), while high-volume tab 0 has only moderate GAUC (0.550087) but very low nDCG@5 (0.062187); tab 6 similarly has GAUC 0.615995 but nDCG@5 0.105841. Rare items are also weak at top five (nDCG@5 0.171736, 249 rows). The zero-positive segment has no evaluable positive ranking target, so its zero top-five metrics are retrospective label-availability artifacts rather than evidence of ranking failure.
priorities.recommended_action: Instrument tab-level serving and inspect candidate-set composition, score distributions, and rank positions for tabs 0, 6, and 8 before any new model experiment. Do not optimize against the zero-positive slice. Use the rare-item slice only as a monitored risk indicator because of limited support.

Do not use quarantined aggregate video-statistics snapshots without per-impression availability timestamps; they present temporal leakage risk.
Do not treat post-score segment diagnostics as independent test estimates or use validation-label-derived user_positive_count as a serving feature. [experiment:1:segment:user_positive_count:zero]
metric_diagnosis: Global GAUC indicates meaningful within-user discrimination, but it does not guarantee strong top-five ranking across traffic contexts. The largest actionable deficits are concentrated in tab slices, where low nDCG@5 can coexist with less-severe GAUC degradation; prioritize candidate and rank-position diagnostics there. Request context is the sole positive screened addition, but its small lift relative to day-to-day variability supports early stopping rather than further feature expansion.
